stemMd:
What number comes next in the sequence?

$2, \; 5, \; 11, \; 23, \; 47, \; \ldots$
explanationMd:
Start with the differences between consecutive terms: $3, 6, 12, 24$. Each difference is double the one before, so the next difference is $48$ and the next term is $47 + 48 = 95$.

The same rule can be seen directly on the terms: each term is twice the previous one plus one ($2 \times 2 + 1 = 5$, $5 \times 2 + 1 = 11$, $11 \times 2 + 1 = 23$, $23 \times 2 + 1 = 47$). Applying it once more gives $47 \times 2 + 1 = 95$. Two descriptions of the same rule agreeing is a good check that you have found it.

What to notice first: when the differences grow quickly, test whether each is a fixed multiple of the previous one before trying anything more elaborate.

distractorRationale.a: This adds the last difference, $24$, a second time. It treats the sequence as if its differences had stopped growing, when every difference so far has doubled.
distractorRationale.b: This doubles $47$ but forgets the $+1$ that every step of the sequence includes. Checking the rule on an earlier step ($5 \times 2 = 10$, not $11$) exposes the slip.
distractorRationale.d: This doubles the next difference, $48$, and reports it as the next term. It confuses the difference with the term itself.
distractorRationale.e: This multiplies by three. No step in the sequence triples: $2 \times 3 = 6$, not $5$.

accessibilityText: A number sequence: 2, 5, 11, 23, 47, followed by a gap for the next term. The question asks for the next number. Five answer choices.
